NDT software in Pittsburgh: what local inspection companies actually deal with

Pittsburgh inspection work comes from four very different customer bases, and most NDT companies in the region serve at least two of them. The Mon Valley steel operations, including U.S. Steel's Clairton coke works, the Edgar Thomson plant in Braddock and the Irvin finishing works, generate steady maintenance and outage inspection: UT thickness on process piping, MT on crane runways and structural members, PT on repaired castings and VT on weld repairs. The Marcellus and Utica shale play to the south and west, with EQT headquartered downtown, keeps gathering lines, compressor stations and midstream fabrication shops busy, mostly RT and PAUT on girth welds. The ethane cracker at Monaca in Beaver County and the Beaver Valley nuclear station at Shippingport bring heavier codes and heavier paperwork. And the region's bridges, hundreds of them across the city and Allegheny County, keep steel-bridge UT and MT crews working for PennDOT and county owners, with more scrutiny on every inspection record since the 2022 Fern Hollow Bridge collapse.

The typical Pittsburgh NDT contractor is a shop of a few dozen technicians with a yard in the North Hills, along the Parkway West or in the Mon Valley. It holds a radioactive materials license from the Pennsylvania DEP Bureau of Radiation Protection (Pennsylvania is an NRC Agreement State), runs a mix of film, CR and DR radiography, and works to an SNT-TC-1A written practice plus whatever the client's own specification adds. The problems are familiar to anyone who has run one of these shops: certification expiries tracked in a spreadsheet that one person understands, instruments that drift out of calibration between jobs, and invoices built from paper timesheets days after the crew is back from site.

ERP for NDT companies in Pittsburgh

The Atlantis ERP solution is a fully customized ERP for NDT and inspection companies. It puts technician certifications, written procedures, equipment calibration, crew dispatch, NDT reports, quoting, timesheets and invoicing into one system, so a Pittsburgh contractor can run a job from the quote to the signed report to the invoice without re-typing anything.

It is set up and supported by Atlantis NDT, founded by Anoop Rayavarapu, an ASNT NDT Level III, so the people configuring it know what a UT calibration table, an IQI placement or a Level III procedure approval actually looks like. It is browser-based, with an offline field app for technicians, and it is configured around your methods, your clients' report formats and your billing structure rather than forcing you into a generic template. Positioning is simple: affordable, accessible and fully customizable, with a demo and quote on request. The sections below walk through each key app and how it applies to the inspection work Pittsburgh contractors actually do. You can also browse every module on the ERP apps page.

Technician certification tracking software for Pittsburgh crews

The Certificates app holds every technician's certifications, with scheme, level, method, certifying body, issue, expiry and renewal dates, and computes the status automatically: active, expiring soon, expired or revoked. Anything inside 90 days appears in the Expiring Soon menu and generates a warning task, so you find out before the client auditor does.

That matters here because Pittsburgh crews move between customers with different demands. A technician on a Beaver Valley outage works under a nuclear-grade quality program; the same person the following week may be on a Marcellus pipeline spread where the operator audits qualification against its own spec, then on a PennDOT bridge job. The ERP records SNT-TC-1A and CP-189 certifications alongside ISO 9712, PCN or CSWIP cards held by technicians you recruit from other countries, with OJT hours, training hours, examination scores (general, specific and practical, against a configurable passing score) and the scanned certificate attached.

Vision tests are tracked separately, covering Jaeger J1/J2 near vision, far vision, colour perception, contrast, examiner and clinic, with their own expiry. A lapsed eye exam grounds a Level II as effectively as an expired cert. The employee NDT profile also stores radiation safety training, radiation badge number and medical fitness expiry, which your radiation safety officer will want in one place when a state inspector visits. Timesheets warn when a technician logs hours without a valid certificate. See the Certificates app for the full field list.

Calibration management software for Pittsburgh NDT equipment

The Asset Management app tracks every flaw detector, thickness gauge, PAUT unit, yoke, probe and radiography accessory by serial number, with calibration frequency, calibration status and next due date. Calibration records capture the provider, certificate number, standard, range, uncertainty, accredited-lab flag and pass, fail or conditional result.

Pittsburgh contractors tend to own a lot of equipment that rotates hard during mill outage season and then sits in the yard. The issue and return workflow, with supervisor and manager approval, records the condition of a unit when it leaves and when it comes back, so a cracked probe wedge or a damaged yoke cable is attributed to a job rather than discovered on the next one. Reservations stop two project managers promising the same PAUT kit to Clairton and to a Washington County compressor station in the same week.

The calibration certificate register holds the lab's accreditation number, valid, expiring or expired status and the PDF itself, with configurable email alerts ahead of expiry. The maintenance log records preventive and corrective work, cleaning, firmware updates and probe replacements with condition before and after. Consumables such as couplant, MT particles, penetrant and developer, PPE and cleaners carry reorder levels and a low-stock flag, so the crew heading to a bridge job on Monday is not short of developer on Tuesday. Details are on the Asset Management app page.

Crew dispatch and scheduling software for Pittsburgh inspection jobs

Team Assignments turns each job into a dispatch record that moves through planned, dispatched, in field, submitted and closed. It blocks double-booking of technicians and of equipment serial numbers, and it warns you when the equipment on an assignment is out of calibration.

Each assignment carries site GPS coordinates and mobilisation and demobilisation dates. That is more useful than it sounds in southwestern Pennsylvania, where a well pad or compressor station often has no street address and a new technician needs exact coordinates to find the access road. The technician availability calendar holds assigned, leave, training, sick and unavailable days, with overlaps blocked, so a Level II booked for recertification training cannot also be dispatched to a mill outage.

Every technician shows a status, current assignment, utilisation percentage and next available date, in calendar, kanban and list views. When the spring mill outages and a nuclear refuelling outage overlap, which happens, you can see at a glance who is free, who is on a long assignment and which RT crews are qualified and in date for the job you have just been asked to cover. Read more on the Team Assignments app.

NDT reporting software for steel, shale and bridge work

The NDT Reports app covers 17 report types, including UT, RT, MT, PT, VT, ECT, IRIS, PAUT, MFL, TOFD, PWHT, PMI, hardness, UT thickness, ferrite, holiday testing and computed radiography, each with its own numbering sequence. Reports move from draft to in progress, review, approved and sent, with inspector, reviewer and approver signatures.

The method-specific fields match the work. RT reports capture source, technique, IQI type and placement, which is what a pipeline operator's auditor checks first. UT reports carry the probe calibration table. PAUT reports record focal laws. UT thickness reports hold readings by direction for mill piping surveys. Weld and job lines record defect type and orientation, and every report closes with an overall result of acceptable, not acceptable or acceptable with remarks. Work order, request, WPS, contract, drawing, procedure and standard references are all captured, and a third-party or authorized inspector can sign on the report.

Many Pittsburgh clients insist on their own report format. Company templates in Excel, Word, PDF or HTML are versioned, and Excel templates are filled automatically by mapping fields to cells. The offline field app works without signal, which covers the river valleys and the inside of mill buildings, stores drafts and photos locally and syncs later. See the NDT Reports app and the standalone Digital Twin Reporting Software.

Written procedures and Level III review

The Procedures app is a controlled register of your written NDT procedures: document number, revision, method, scope, material, applicable standard such as ASME Section V, acceptance criteria and the procedure text or uploaded file. Each revision moves through draft, submitted, reviewed, approved and published, with prepared, reviewed and approved by names and dates.

Approved revisions are locked and a snapshot of every revision is kept, so when a client asks which revision of your UT shear-wave procedure was in force on a job last March, you can show it. Rejections carry a reason. Approvers get email notifications and reminders for pending approvals, which helps when your Level III is on site for a week. An AI-assisted first draft can speed up a new procedure, for example a bridge-specific MT procedure, but a Level III still reviews and approves every revision. See the Procedures app.

NDT quoting and invoicing software for Pittsburgh contractors

Quotations carry job type, site, project dates and applicable codes, with NDT service products flagged by method and category, a branded PDF and online acceptance and signature that converts straight into a sales order. Invoices carry the NDT project, job or PO number, site, invoice type and industry sector, with separate subtotals for labour, equipment and consumables.

Invoice lines hold cost centre, method, equipment serial, technician, billing basis and days or hours. Timesheets record work type (inspection, travel, standby, setup), method, site, client, equipment serial, a billable flag and an overtime multiplier, and approved hours feed billing directly. That removes the Friday-afternoon job of reconciling a week of paper timesheets against a steel mill's PO lines. Standby hours waiting for a permit at a mill, which are easy to lose on paper, are recorded as their own work type. The financial dashboard shows revenue, cost of sales, gross margin, operating expenses, EBITDA, outstanding invoices, bills and expenses over a 12-month view. Links: Quotations, Invoicing, Timesheets.

Radiography vehicles, field expenses and consumables

Radiography crews in western Pennsylvania drive a lot of miles between well pads, mills and bridge sites. The Fleet app records each vehicle's purpose, whether it can carry radioactive sources, and its transport licence number and expiry, and assigns vehicles to projects and drivers with dates and mileage. Combined with the radiation badge and radiation safety training fields on each technician, it gives your RSO a clearer picture of who and what went where.

Expenses handles per diems, fuel, hotel nights and other field costs and allows them to be re-billed to the job. Purchase records vendor types such as OEM, dealer and calibration lab, with an accredited-lab flag, accreditation number and expiry, and order lines linked to a specific equipment serial, so a probe replacement is tied to the instrument it went into. See Fleet, Expenses and Purchase.

Inspection management software in Pittsburgh: how implementation works

Implementation is done remotely by the Atlantis team, with working sessions scheduled around your shifts rather than in the middle of an outage. A typical sequence looks like this:

  1. Discovery: your methods, clients, report formats, written practice, billing structure and the systems you already use.
  2. Data load: technicians, certifications, vision tests, equipment serials and calibration certificates imported from your existing spreadsheets.
  3. Templates: your report and quotation formats rebuilt, including client-specific Excel reports mapped cell by cell.
  4. Integrations: the open REST API connects to QuickBooks, NetSuite, SAP, Maximo or any system that accepts API connections, scoped per implementation.
  5. Training and go-live: office staff first, then field technicians on the offline app, ideally in a quieter month before the spring outage season.

Anything your operation needs that is not a built-in feature, such as a particular client's approval step or a custom dashboard, is configured during implementation. To discuss a timeline, ask for a Pittsburgh implementation plan.

Frequently asked questions

What is the best NDT software for a Pittsburgh inspection company?

The best fit is software that covers certifications, calibration, dispatch, reports and invoicing in one place. The Atlantis ERP does that and is configured around your methods and clients, which suits contractors serving steel, shale, nuclear and bridge work at the same time.

Can the ERP track certifications for nuclear, pipeline and bridge clients separately?

Yes. Each technician can hold several certifications by scheme, method, level and industry sector, each with its own dates and status, plus vision tests and radiation safety details. Client-specific qualification rules are configured during implementation.

Does the field app work at well pads and inside mill buildings without signal?

Yes. The offline field app stores drafts and photos on the device and syncs when a connection returns, with photo capture, on-screen signature and PDF preview.

Can it produce reports in our clients' own Excel formats?

Yes. Versioned Excel templates are filled automatically by mapping report fields to cells, alongside Word, PDF and HTML templates with your logo, header and footer.

The Atlantis ERP has an open REST API and integrates with QuickBooks, NetSuite, SAP, Maximo or any system that accepts API connections. The exact scope is agreed per implementation.

Pricing is a quote on request, based on the apps you need and your team size. The positioning is affordable and accessible for small and mid-size contractors. Ask for a quote.
